about: SMTP command decisions: application sends, the customer life and RFC Appendix D; command semantics are the byte-stream front, not HTTP CRUD.

decisions.demand: journeys/demand.json; customer life and RFC 5321 Appendix D
decisions.why: The connection front frames and answers this command, consulting the session machines for state moves; SMTP replies cannot be HTTP CRUD. Nodemailer's transport.verify() and sendMail() in journeys/first-use.json send-invite.mjs open the session on the 220 greeting.

decisions.demand: journeys/demand.json; customer life and RFC 5321 Appendix D
decisions.why: The connection front frames and answers this command, consulting the session machines for state moves; SMTP replies cannot be HTTP CRUD. The customer entry's transport.verify() and sendMail() (first-use.json send-invite.mjs) greet with EHLO; verify resolving true asserts the session.

decisions.demand: journeys/demand.json; customer life and RFC 5321 Appendix D
decisions.why: The connection front frames and answers this command, consulting the session machines for state moves; SMTP replies cannot be HTTP CRUD. The customer entry's sendMail (first-use.json send-invite.mjs) sends a RCPT for each of its two recipients; info.accepted holding both and info.rejected none asserts them.

decisions.demand: journeys/demand.json; customer life and RFC 5321 Appendix D
decisions.why: The connection front frames and answers this command, consulting the session machines for state moves; SMTP replies cannot be HTTP CRUD. The customer entry's sendMail (first-use.json send-invite.mjs) sends the multipart invitation (html, text, calendar event, List-Unsubscribe headers); info.response 250 and its message id assert the acceptance.

decisions.demand: the World's own door, POST /_twin/relay: { hostname?, auth?: { username, password }, senderDomains?, relayDomains?, maxSize?, localRecipients? }: the relay's policy, as its operator configures it; an empty body makes it an open relay
decisions.why: { hostname?, auth?: { username, password }, senderDomains?, relayDomains?, maxSize?, localRecipients? }: the relay's policy, as its operator configures it; an empty body makes it an open relay, which no vendor API makes.
